items.originalTitle: Williams, Aston Martin among new F1 liveries for Las Vegas GP as Acura "replaces" Honda
detailZh: 威廉姆斯和阿斯顿·马丁等车队将为拉斯维加斯大奖赛推出全新赛车涂装，而阿库拉（Acura）取代了本田（Honda）
一级方程式车队将为即将到来的拉斯维加斯大奖赛推出独一无二的赛车涂装，阿斯顿·马丁将推广本田的性能品牌阿库拉
威廉姆斯和阿斯顿·马丁是本周拉斯维加斯大奖赛中涂装焕新的F1车队之一
一级方程式赛事将前往拉斯维加斯参加其在美国的三场比赛中的第三场，娱乐之都迅速成为系列赛中对于车队及其合作伙伴来说的关键商业周末。
因此，本周有几支车队推出了定制涂装，威廉姆斯车队将阿隆索和萨因斯的FW48赛车涂装为蓝色铬色。
与此同时，阿斯顿·马丁将所有主要标志从动力单元合作伙伴本田更换为Acura的标志，Acura是本田的豪华品牌，主要活跃在北美地区。
作为本田F1车队长期接管美国市场的一部分，Acura将装饰AMR-26赛车的车头、发动机罩和车手赛车服。
根据赞助商CoreWeave的要求，费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔的赛车也将车头、侧箱和发动机罩增加白色装饰。
阿尔法·罗密欧车队将在侧箱上增加额外的粉色品牌标识，以展示即将离任的赞助商BWT。
detailEn: Williams, Aston Martin among new F1 liveries for Las Vegas GP as Acura "replaces" Honda
Formula 1 teams are rolling out one-off liveries for Formula 1's Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Aston Martin promoting Honda's performance brand Acura
Williams and Aston Martin are among the F1 teams to have revamped their car liveries for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix.
F1 heads to Las Vegas for its third of three US races, with the entertainment capital having quickly become one of the series' key commercial weekends for teams and their partners.
As a result, several teams are rolling out bespoke liveries this week, with Williams deploying a blue chrome livery on the FW48 races by Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz.
Meanwhile, Aston Martin is replaces all of its main logos of power unit partner Honda with those of Acura, Honda's luxury brand which is primarily active in North America.
Acura will adorn the nose, engine cover and driver race suits of the AMR-26 as part of a long line of US takeovers for Honda's F1 teams.
Fernando Alonso's and Lance Stroll's cars will also receive additional notes of white on the nose, sidepod and engine cover at the behest of sponsor CoreWeave.
The Alpine team will meanwhile feature additional pink branding on the sidepod for outgoing title sponsor BWT.

items.originalTitle: Lando Norris's LN4 Fusion signs former Red Bull junior Oliver Goethe as its first F2 driver
detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯的LN4融合车队签下了前红牛青训车队车手奥利弗·戈特，作为其首个F2车手
戈特将从MP车队加入，开始他的第三个F2赛季，今年已经获得了两次领奖台位置
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事
兰多·诺里斯的新青训车队LN4融合签下了前红牛青训车队车手奥利弗·戈特，作为2027年F2赛季的首位车手
22岁的车手将从MP Motorsport转会至F2，这是他第三个赛季参加F2，此前他已经在本年度获得了两次领奖台的成绩。
LN4 Fusion车队在上个月获得了F2的参赛资格，成为锦标赛下三个赛季周期中唯一的新车队。该车队由麦凯轮一级方程式车队的车手在九月创立，并将同时运营F3、意大利F4和英国F4的比赛车辆。
戈特海姆曾是红牛青训项目的成员两年，于2025年底离开。在晋升至F2之前，他在2022年赢得了11场胜利，获得了欧罗巴公式开放赛冠军，并在FIA F3中赢得了两场比赛。
在宣布这笔交易时，LN4 Fusion首席执行官丹·理查兹表示，德国车手的经验使他成为车队第一个赛季的最佳选择。
"奥利弗是我们队的绝佳选择。他对赛车、赛道和锦标赛都非常了解，他今年的领奖台表现也显示他已经采取了必要的步骤来争夺领奖台，”理查兹说。
"我们希望为他提供他所需要的环境和支持，以继续朝着他的最终目标迈进，并且我们相信，我们一起可以有一个强劲的赛季，”戈特说。
戈特表示，他认为2027年可能是他争夺冠军的最佳机会。
"我非常激动能够加入LN4 Fusion车队参加2027赛季！这是一个非常激动人心的项目，我迫不及待地想要成为其中的一员。我真心觉得明年可能会是我的年份，我决心充分利用这次机会，”他说。
“作为德国赛车运动团队与奥迪合作的一部分，我已经在奥迪的F1模拟器中完成了几节练习，这让我在即将到来的赛季之前获得了有用的经验和赛道洞察。”
LN4 Fusion的欧洲运营将由Prema车队的前成员领导，前Prema老板Rene Rosin担任顾问和车队负责人，前Prema技术总监Guillaume Capietto担任赛车总监。
detailEn: Lando Norris's LN4 Fusion signs former Red Bull junior Oliver Goethe as its first F2 driver
Goethe will join from MP Motorsport for his third F2 season after two podiums this year
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Lando Norris's new junior team LN4 Fusion has signed former Red Bull junior Oliver Goethe as its first driver for the 2027 Formula 2 season.
The 22-year-old will make the move from MP Motorsport for his third season in F2, after celebrating two podium finishes so far this year.

LN4 Fusion was granted an entry to F2 last month, as the only new team for the championship's next three-year cycle. The McLaren Formula 1 driver launched the team in September, and it will also run cars in Formula 3, Italian Formula 4 and British F4.

Goethe was part of Red Bull's junior programme for two years before leaving at the end of 2025. Before stepping up to F2, he won the Euroformula Open title in 2022 with 11 victories, and took two wins in FIA Formula 3.
Announcing the deal, LN4 Fusion chief executive Dan Richards said the German's experience made him the right choice for the team's first season.

"Oliver is a great choice for our team. He knows the car, the tracks and the championship well, and his podiums this year show that he has taken the steps needed to fight at the front," Richards said.
"We want to give him the environment and support he needs to continue making progress towards his ultimate goal, and we are confident that together we can have a strong season."
Goethe said he believes 2027 could be his best chance yet to fight for the title.

"I'm absolutely thrilled to be joining LN4 Fusion for the 2027 season! It's a really exciting project, and I can't wait to be part of it. I genuinely feel that next year could be my year, and I'm determined to make the most of this opportunity," he said.

"As part of the cooperation between Motorsport Team Germany and Audi, I have already completed several sessions in Audi's F1 simulator, gaining useful experience and insight into the tracks ahead of the upcoming season."

LN4 Fusion's European operation will be led by former members of the Prema team, with ex-Prema boss Rene Rosin on board as a consultant and team principal, and former Prema technical chief Guillaume Capietto as racing director.

items.originalTitle: Lando Norris: F1 needs better rain tyres as wet Las Vegas would be "scary"
items.summaryEn: World champion Lando Norris hopes Pirelli will introduce much-improved rain tyres in 2027, as he believes the current range would not work properly at a low-downforce circuit like Las Vegas.
detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯：F1需要更好的雨胎，拉斯维加斯雨战会“很吓人”
领先的F1车手们希望倍耐力能对其湿地轮胎系列做出重大改进
世界冠军兰多·诺里斯希望F1轮胎供应商倍耐力在2027年推出大幅改进的雨胎，因为他预计现有雨胎在拉斯维加斯这类低下压力赛道上无法正常工作。
在马来西亚和新加坡经历部分受雨水影响的比赛周末后，F1的2026款赛车在巴西大奖赛首次经历真正意义上的湿地排位赛和正赛，倍耐力的全雨胎和半雨胎配方都在圣保罗接受了测试。排位赛因多个弯道积水而中断超过一小时，打滑（aquaplaning）风险促使车手在Q1使用全雨胎，随后换上半雨胎。
这场比赛在湿地胎下开始并结束，中间有一段干燥期，消除了此前对2026代赛车在湿滑条件下表现的担忧。但尽管巴西站呈现了一场精彩的表演，倍耐力的雨胎在正确的工作窗口内基本按预期工作，车手们仍然认为今年的硬质湿地胎需要在低温性能上改进，因为他们在 赛段开始时和前往发车格的圈中难以将赛车保持在赛道上。
由于英特拉格斯是赛历上最容易让轮胎进入工作范围的赛道之一，几位车手担心倍耐力的产品在并非如此的赛道上不够稳健，比如即将到来的拉斯维加斯街道赛道。
国际汽联的官方天气预报尚未公布，但其他预测显示周四晚间第一节自由练习的降雨概率超过50%，之后条件更可能干燥。
由于拉斯维加斯周末气温远低于10摄氏度，且赛道缺乏任何高速弯道来给轮胎施加横向负荷，迈凯伦车手诺里斯表示湿地练习会相当“可怕”，因为湿地胎在太冷时无法工作。
当被 Motorsport.com 问及对本规则周期首个真正湿地周末的评判时，诺里斯说：“轮胎变冷时，情况相当糟糕。在前往发车格的圈里，当它们变得非常冷时，感觉糟透了。如果进入合适的工作窗口，它们就很好。所以，我认为可怕的时刻是如果你去拉斯维加斯却无法让轮胎升温。你需要比我们这里好得多的轮胎，因为那会非常糟糕。”
巴西站亚军马克斯·维斯塔潘补充道：“我认为主要是工作范围有点太小了。热的时候还可以，但冷的时候，它们真的像石头一样。这是我们需要努力解决的问题，要在全雨胎（extreme wet）和半雨胎（intermediates）上生成更大的工作范围。我认为这会大大有助于更好地让轮胎进入工作状态，然后甚至能在更大的雨中行驶。”
威廉姆斯车手卡洛斯·塞恩斯也认为倍耐力的整个轮胎系列都需要改进。“我认为雨胎和半雨胎的水平不够好，我们需要与倍耐力合作找到更好的轮胎，因为在混合条件下，半雨胎在后轮仍然是非常弱的轮胎；等它升温时，前轮已经不行了。
“而全雨胎说实话，[在排位赛中]我们出现了大量水滑，后轮抓地力严重不足，所以这两款轮胎仍然缺少一些开发。”
倍耐力面临一项艰巨任务：要为F1 2026年全新规则套件开发雨胎，这些规则包含高扭矩动力单元和主动空气动力学，会给轮胎施加巨大作用力。与此同时，倍耐力还在追逐一个不断变化的目标，即车队究竟能产生多少下压力，而赛季中激烈的研发进展已经超出了这家供应商的预期。
在休赛期，国际汽联在湿地条件下实施了一种部分直道模式以缓解安全担忧，现在只有前翼会被激活。随后在4月，管理机构还降低了湿地条件下的电力输出。据信这两项措施对2026年赛车在湿地中相对安全地比赛的能力产生了很大影响，但它们显然是在倍耐力不得不确定其2026年轮胎系列之后才出台的。
F1首次真正使用全雨胎和半雨胎进行测试来得如此之晚，以至于倍耐力无法将巴西站的教训纳入2027年的考量，因为这家意大利轮胎制造商已经敲定了下赛季的认证。
但在今年早些时候的早期开发工作之后，倍耐力得以在上个月于马尼库尔进行关键的湿地测试，试验其在2026年全年研发的各种解决方案。在这条法国赛道上，梅赛德斯储备车手弗雷德里克·维斯蒂进行了为期两天的测试，其中一天在湿地条件下测试了多种采用不同配方和结构的新型半雨胎。
倍耐力的赛道工程主管西蒙内·贝拉在墨西哥表示：“我们测试了一些方案，尤其是针对半雨胎的方案，最终得到了我们想在下个赛季引入的不错选择。可以肯定的是，我们的想法是改进明年的雨胎产品。”
“我们在配方上做了工作，在胎面厚度上做了工作，也在不同结构上做了工作。所以，我们在轮胎的不同方面做了大量工作，希望把最佳方案结合起来。我们现在正在处理数据，接下来将对新的雨胎配方规格进行认证。”
在圣保罗排位赛后，倍耐力赛车运动负责人达里奥·马拉富斯基坚称，公司已为2027年“取得了一些进展”。他说：“当然，我们非常认真地对待了一些车手的质疑，并在这一年里推进了研发。我们知道总有改进的空间，我们相信我们为明年向前迈出了一些步伐。”
“获得这些信息（来自巴西）非常有价值。遗憾的是，它直到赛季末才出现。我们已经完成了明年的雨胎研发。我不想透露明年雨胎会发生什么，但我们是根据赛季初掌握的信息以及我们在铃鹿进行的一些测试来完成雨胎研发的，所以这对我们来说有助于确定今年的优先事项。”
“我们在马尼库尔进行了一次积极的测试，很快我们就会公布这次湿地测试的结果。”
detailEn: Lando Norris: F1 needs better rain tyres as wet Las Vegas would be "scary"
Leading Formula 1 drivers are hoping Pirelli can make significant improvements to its wet-weather range of tyres

World champion Lando Norris hopes Formula 1 tyre supplier Pirelli will field much-improved rain tyres in 2027 as he expects the current range won't work properly at a low-downforce circuit like Las Vegas.

Following partially rain-affected weekends in Malaysia and Singapore, F1's 2026 cars went through their first proper qualifying and grand prix held in wet conditions at the Brazilian Grand Prix, with both Pirelli's full wet and intermediate compounds being put to the test at Sao Paulo. Qualifying had to be halted for over an hour due to standing water in several corners, with the risk of aquaplaning prompting drivers to run full-wet tyres in Q1 before switching to intermediates.

The race both started and finished on intermediates, with a dry middle spell, dispelling early fears over how the 2026 generation of cars would run in the wet. But while Brazil put on an entertaining spectacle and Pirelli's rain tyres largely worked as expected in the right operating window, drivers still felt this year's stiffer intermediates need work on how they perform in low temperatures as they struggled to keep their cars on the track at the start of a stint and on laps to the grid.

With Interlagos being one of the easiest circuits on the calendar to get tyres into the working range, several drivers voiced concerns that Pirelli's offering won't be robust enough on circuits where that isn't the case, like the upcoming Las Vegas street circuit.

The FIA's official weather forecast is not available yet, but other predictions suggest the chance of rain is over 50% for Free Practice 1 on Thursday evening, with conditions more likely to be dry after that.

With temperatures dipping well below 10C over the Vegas weekend and the circuit lacking any high-speed corners to put lateral load into the tyres, McLaren driver Norris said a wet practice would be quite "scary" because the intermediates don't work when they're too cold.

"When the tyres get cold, it's pretty nasty," Norris said when asked by Motorsport.com for his verdict on F1's first proper wet-weather weekend of this rules cycle. "On laps to the grid, when they get very cold, they felt horrible. If they get into a good window, they're good. So, I think the scary times are if you go to Vegas and you can't get any tyre temperature. You need a much better tyre than what we have here because that's going to be horrible."

Brazil runner-up Max Verstappen added: "I think it's mainly that the working range is a bit too small. When they're hot, it's okay, but when they're cold, they're really like a rock. That's something that we need to try and work on, to generate a bigger working range on the extreme wet [tyres] and the intermediates. I think that would help a lot with switching on the tyre better and then being able to run even in heavier rain."

Williams driver Carlos Sainz also felt Pirelli's entire range needed improvements. "I think the level of the wet and the inter is not good enough and we need to work with Pirelli on finding a better tyre because in the mixed conditions the inter is still a very weak tyre at the rear; by the time it warms up the front is gone.
"And the extreme honestly, [in qualifying] we had so much aquaplaning and a big lack of rear grip, so still missing a bit of development on these two tyres."

Pirelli faced a difficult task developing rain tyres for F1 2026's all-new regulations suite with their high-torque power units and active aerodynamics, putting significant forces through the rubber. It meanwhile chased a moving target of just how much downforce the teams would be able to generate, with fierce in-season development already ahead of the supplier's projections.

Over the off-season the FIA implemented a partial Straight Mode in the wet to ease safety concerns, with only the front wing now being activated. Then, in April, the governing body also reduced electric output in wet conditions. Those two measures are believed to have made a big difference to the 2026 cars' ability to race in the wet relatively safely, but they obviously arrived well after Pirelli had to define its 2026 tyre range.

F1's first proper running on both the extreme wet tyres and intermediates is coming so late in the season that Pirelli can't take Brazil's lessons into account for 2027, as the Italian tyre manufacturer has already finalised its homologations for next season.

But following earlier development work at the start of the year, it was able to conduct crucial wet-weather testing in Magny-Cours last month, trialling the various solutions it worked on over the course of 2026. At the French circuit, Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti conduced two days of testing, including one day in the wet to trial various new intermediate tyres featuring different compounds and constructions.

"We tested some solutions, especially for the intermediates, and we ended up with good options that we would like to introduce for next season," Pirelli's trackside engineering chief Simone Berra said in Mexico. "For sure the idea is to improve the wet-weather product for next year.

"We worked on the compounds, we worked on the tread thickness, we also worked on different structures. So, we worked a lot on different tyre aspects and we would like to combine the best solutions. We are working on the data now and we are going to homologate new wet-weather compound specifications."

Speaking after qualifying in Sao Paulo, Pirelli's head of motorsport Dario Marrafuschi was adamant the company has "made some steps" for 2027. "Of course, we took quite seriously the scepticism from some drivers, and we addressed the development during the year. We know there is always room for improvement and we believe we made some steps ahead for next year," he said.

"It is a great value having this information [from Brazil]. Unfortunately, it is coming only towards the end of the season. We have already closed the wet development for next year. I don't want to disclose what will happen on the wet next year, but we made the wet development based on the information we had at the beginning of the season and some of the testing we did in Suzuka, so that was good for us to address the priorities for this year.
"We had a positive test in Magny-Cours, and quite [soon] we will be disclosing the outcome of this wet test."

detailZh: Toto Wolff预测基米·安东内利将在意大利比迈克尔·舒马赫更受欢迎

梅赛德斯车队负责人Toto Wolff在发表大胆言论方面并不陌生，但对他对基米·安东内利的受欢迎程度的最新评估可能会让忠实的法拉利粉丝感到震惊。
在安东内利在墨西哥城赢得历史性的2026年车手锦标赛胜利后，Wolff接受了德国出版物BILD的独家采访。当对话转向这位20岁天才新星日益增长的星光时，Wolff被问及他的年轻车手是否注定在意大利比七届世界冠军迈克尔·舒马赫更受欢迎。
"绝对是这样！他是意大利人，"Wolff直率地回答。
几十年来，迈克尔·舒马赫在意大利被广泛视为不可触及的神，为斯库德利亚赢得了五个连续的世界冠军。相比之下，安东内利目前为梅赛德斯车队效力，这个车队在历史上被视为法拉利的头号竞争对手。
Wolff 认为，尽管安东内利不是法拉利的车手，但他的意大利血统和真实个性使他超越了团队忠诚。
“是的，但基米凭借他自然的方式和成功所取得的成就，是意大利当然仍然对他的国家队，法拉利——但同时也向这个小意大利敞开了心扉，”Wolff 解释道。
为了证明他的观点，Wolff 直接指出了2026年意大利大奖赛在蒙扎的气氛。根据梅赛德斯老板的说法，传奇的tifosi 主动庆祝了安东内利在他们家乡制造商的成功。
“现在tifosi 穿着法拉利的球衣，戴着梅赛德斯帽子，”Wolff 断言。“蒙扎是完美的例子。观众实际上很伤心，两位红色赛车都没有赢得第一，但他们很高兴，他们的一个基米，站在了领奖台的最顶端。”
安东内利成功锁定2026年冠军，并巩固了自己自1953年阿尔贝托·阿斯卡里以来首位意大利一级方程式世界冠军的地位，他在国内的受欢迎程度预计只会增长——即使他继续在终点线前击败法拉利。

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff is no stranger to making bold statements, but his latest assessment of Kimi Antonelli's popularity might actually shock the dedicated Ferrari fanbase.

Following Antonelli's historic 2026 drivers' championship victory in Mexico City, Wolff sat down for an exclusive interview with the German publication BILD. When the conversation shifted to the 20-year-old prodigy's exploding star power, Wolff was asked if his young driver was destined to become more popular in Italy than seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher.
"Absolutely! He is Italian," Wolff bluntly replied.

For decades, Michael Schumacher has been widely considered an untouchable deity in Italy, having secured five consecutive world championships for the Scuderia. In contrast, Antonelli currently races for Mercedes, a team historically viewed as one of Ferrari's primary rivals.
Wolff argued that, although Antonelli is not a Ferrari driver, his Italian heritage and authentic personality have allowed him to transcend team loyalty.

"Yes, but what Kimi has achieved through his natural manner and success is that Italy is, of course, still feverish for his national team, Ferrari - but has also opened its heart and soul to this little Italian," Wolff explained.

To prove his point, Wolff pointed directly to the atmosphere at the 2026 Italian Grand Prix in Monza. According to the Mercedes boss, the legendary Tifosi actively celebrated Antonelli's success over their own hometown constructor.

"The Tifosi are now wearing the Ferrari shirt with a Mercedes cap," Wolff claimed. "Monza was the perfect example. The spectators were actually sad that neither of the two red racers came in first, but they were pleased that Kimi, one of their own, was at the very top of the podium."

With Antonelli successfully locking down the 2026 championship and cementing himself as the first Italian F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, his popularity at home is only expected to grow - even if he continues to beat the Ferraris to the finish line.

At the height of their bitter championship battles, the idea of Christian Horner sending Toto Wolff a warm congratulatory text would have seemed entirely fictional to most Formula 1 fans. "Yes, but that didn't surprise me," Wolff stated. "Christian and I have a respectful relationship. That was already the case back then."

When Wolff made the decision to replace Ferrari-bound Lewis Hamilton with Antonelli, critics actively questioned if the teenager was ready for the immense pressure of a championship-calibre team. Having worked with a similar junior driver pipeline during his time at Red Bull, Horner reached out to commend Wolff for taking that gamble.
When asked to reveal the exact contents of the text message, Wolff shared Horner's private words.
"'Congratulations. Kimi was incredible this year and respect for you giving him your back at such a young age,'" Horner wrote.

The exchange reveals a rare moment of camaraderie between the two most dominant team bosses of the modern turbo-hybrid era, underscoring that their intense on-track warfare was ultimately underpinned by professional respect.

麦凯轮赛车首席执行官Zak Brown将2016年加入的团队描述为“一个非常恶劣的环境”，并将多年来的赛道内外不佳成绩归咎于领导层的频繁更迭。
这位美国人十年前加入迈凯轮车队，当时车队股东与罗恩·邓恩分道扬镳，之后他带领车队从车队末尾的排名恢复到2024年和2025年的车队制造商锦标赛。
在接受RACER采访时，布朗表示，当他最初走进车队时，并没有意识到问题的严重性。
“那是一个非常有毒的环境。问题始于领导层的真正不协调以及领导力的缺乏。在六年的时间里，你有了五位不同的老板，”布朗说。
“这在任何商业中都是灾难的配方。如果你在领导层有旋转门，那么团队不知道该跟随谁。这会滋生信任的缺失，并在组织中产生毒性。”
他补充说，对车队的影响是显而易见的。
每个人都处于保护自己、指责他人的模式。这是一个糟糕的环境。这种糟糕的环境体现在糟糕的赛道成绩、缺乏赞助、缺乏粉丝参与和非常不满意的员工队伍。
兰多·诺里斯，麦凯轮，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，麦凯轮，安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯
布朗承认他最初相信车队自己的解释，即其发动机合作伙伴是主要问题。当沃金团队将本田换成雷诺后，从2017年的车队 constructors' championship 第9位跃升至2018年的第6位，但他表示，这仅仅表明问题有多深。
“我知道在我们当时拥有的1,200人中，我们可能只需要修复其中大约20人。在我心中，毫无疑问，我们有1,100人在那里赢得了许多比赛和冠军。我们需要领导团队的重置，”他说。
在2024年和2025年，麦凯轮车队赢得了车队冠军，兰多·诺里斯在2025年赢得了车手冠军之后，本赛季对布朗领导的车队来说更加艰难。麦凯轮车队在车队积分榜上排名第四，落后红牛17分，尽管诺里斯赢得了三场比赛。
“我们在2024年和2025年赢得了比赛，今年也赢得了比赛，但这并不赋予我们在2027年任何东西。我们必须赢得它，”布朗说。
detailEn: Zak Brown recalls McLaren's "very toxic environment" after joining team in 2016
The McLaren CEO says most of the team's 1,200 staff were not the problem
For McLaren fans. Papaya news from Woking, with the latest on the drivers, the car, team strategy and every race weekend.
McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown has described the team he joined in 2016 as "a very toxic environment", blaming a revolving door of leaders for years of poor results on and off the track.

The American arrived at McLaren a decade ago, after the team's shareholders parted ways with Ron Dennis, and went on to lead its recovery from the back of the grid to the 2024 and 2025 constructors' championships.
Speaking to RACER, Brown said he had not realised the scale of the problems when he first walked in.
"It was a very toxic environment. It started with a real lack of alignment of the leadership as well as a lack of leadership. You had five different bosses in six years," Brown said.

"That's a recipe for disaster in any business. If you have a revolving door at the leadership level, then the team don't know who to follow. That breeds a lack of trust and breeds toxicity inside an organisation."
He added that the effect on the team was clear to see.

"Everyone was in cover-their-ass mode and blame mode. It was a terrible environment. That manifested itself in terrible on-track results, lack of sponsorship, lack of fan engagement and a very unsatisfied workforce."
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

Brown admitted he had initially believed the team's own explanation that its engine partner was the main problem. When the Woking outfit replaced Honda with Renault, it moved from ninth in the constructors' championship in 2017 to sixth in 2018, but he said that only showed how much deeper the issues ran.

"I knew out of the 1,200 people that we had at the time that we probably only needed to fix about 20 of them. There was no doubt in my mind that we had 1,100 people there who had won a lot of races and championships. It needed the leadership team reset," he said.

After McLaren won the constructors' title in both 2024 and 2025 and Lando Norris secured the drivers' championship in 2025, this season has been tougher for the Brown-led team. McLaren is fourth in the constructors' standings, 17 points behind Red Bull, although Norris has won three races.
"The fact that we won in 2024 and 2025 and that we have won races this year, that doesn't entitle us to anything in 2027. We have got to earn it," Brown said.

早在2023年，刘易斯·汉密尔顿就解释了他的使命：在赛车运动领域改变来自服务不足社区的年轻人的生活。
Mission 44 的报告提出了三项建议。
第一项是每年公布一份覆盖整个赛车运动的图景，按性别、族裔和社会经济背景说明谁加入、谁晋升、谁离开。
第二项，报告呼吁将人才投资——首先是学徒薪资——排除在赛车运动的预算帽之外，并且 F1、国际汽联、各车队和商业合作伙伴随后“在未来五年内投入至少 5000 万英镑的新资金，帮助来自代表性不足背景的年轻人进入赛车运动职业，并支持他们留下来”。
第三项建议是，每支车队都应承诺“每年公布一定数量的带薪、可及的职业生涯早期岗位，到 2030 年建成数千条进入赛车运动的带薪通道”，同时“对自动化筛选进行偏见测试并披露其使用情况”。
汉密尔顿补充道：“所以这就是我的请求。致每一位车队领队、每一位首席执行官，以及一级方程式和FIA的领导者们：让我们把这份报告中的三项建议付诸实施。”
F1上个月发布了其首份全运动社会影响报告。
报告显示，2025年，来自71个国家的超过50万年轻人参与并受益于一级方程式在教育和社区外展方面的项目，同时超过2500名年轻人在F1赛道参加了活动。
报告还宣布将其工程奖学金延长三年，至少持续到2028/29学年，并承诺再提供240万英镑的资金。
该报道还补充称，这项运动将“加强其在治理、衡量和报告方面的方法，以更好地理解成果、分享进展，并最大化其社会影响工作的长期价值”。
一位F1发言人表示：“我们为那些有助于激励下一代一级方程式车手和参与者的项目和倡议感到自豪，也为它们如何持续增加我们这项运动中的参与机会和可及性感到自豪。
“在汉密尔顿委员会提出建议之后，这项运动于2024年签署了其有史以来第一份多元与包容（D&I）宪章，并在2025年首次开展了全运动范围的数据收集工作，以了解我们社会影响项目的全球覆盖情况。
“这表明，仅在2025赛季，全球就有超过50万名年轻人参与了教育、STEM和激励项目，并且我们这项运动中提供了超过1000个结构化的技能和人才发展机会。
“随着一级方程式赛车在全球舞台上的持续发展，我们深化和演进社会影响力的雄心也在不断增强。我们与F1各车队、国际汽联以及这项运动的广大成员一道，致力于在这一基础上继续建设，并期待分享我们下一阶段的工作。”
在表达对未来取得更多进展的希望时，汉密尔顿表示：“从工程奖学金和多元与包容宪章，到激励超过50万名年轻人，我们帮助推动了真正的进展。我为我们所取得的成就感到自豪，但我们远未完成。”
“一级方程式赛车正在激励全世界数百万年轻人。但如果没有机会，激励就毫无意义。我们不能告诉年轻人要胸怀大志，然后当他们试图将这些梦想变为现实时却不打开大门。”
“F1、国际汽联和每支车队都必须加大力度、加快步伐。我们需要真正的投资、更多的机会和更强的问责制。我们已经证明改变是可能的。现在我们需要走得更远。人才就在那里，而我们这项运动的未来取决于能否释放他们的潜力。”

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton says work improving diversity in F1 'nowhere near finished' as Mission 44 outlines recommendations for further change

The seven-time champion's Mission 44 foundation outlines three recommendations to help more young people from under-represented backgrounds get into and stay in F1; Hamilton "heartened" by changes seen in the sport since 2021 and "proud of what we've achieved" and believes more can be done

Lewis Hamilton says Formula 1 has "shown that change is possible" to improve diversity in the sport over the past five years and "now we need to go further" in increasing opportunities for the next generation.

Five years after the Hamilton Commission made its recommendations for change, the seven-time world champion's Mission 44 foundation released a new report titled 'Igniting Inclusion' reviewing progress for Black people, women and young people from lower-income backgrounds.

The report acknowledged the "significant steps forward" made in the sport since 2021, which include the signing of a diversity and inclusion charter - which all 11 teams, F1 and the FIA are signatories to - the creation of an engineering scholarship and the launch of F1 Academy. The sport also published its first social impact report last month.

Hamilton welcomed those achievements and also feels "there is much still to do".

"I want to start by saying thank you. To the teams, to Formula 1 and to the FIA, who signed the first Diversity and Inclusion Charter in the history of this sport," said the Ferrari driver in the report.

"To the people inside the teams who built scholarships, placements and mentoring schemes that did not exist in 2021. To the teachers, charities and volunteers who take the sport into classrooms every week.
"When I walk through the paddock now, I see more women, more Black and Brown faces, more people who look like the fans in the grandstands than at any point since I started.
"That is heartening, and the people behind it deserve credit. And yet, there is much still to do.
"We have opened the door, but we have not yet learned to count how many people walk through it, or how many stay.

"The sport's first Social Impact Report shows how much is happening. This report asks what it adds up to. This is a sport that measures performance to the thousandth of a second. We can measure this too."
Back in 2023, Lewis Hamilton explained his mission to transform the lives of young people from underserved communities in the world of motorsport
Mission 44's report makes three recommendations.
The first is for the publication of one sport-wide picture each year of who joins, who is promoted and who leaves, by gender, ethnicity and socio-economic background.

Secondly, the report calls for talent investment, starting with apprentice salaries, to be excluded from the sport's budget cap and that F1, the FIA, the teams and commercial partners then "invest at least £50m of new money over the next five years in helping young people from under-represented backgrounds into motorsport careers, and supporting them to stay".

The third recommendation is for every team to commit to "a published number of paid, accessible early-career places each year, building thousands of paid routes into motorsport by 2030", while "automated screening is tested for bias and its use disclosed".
Hamilton added: "So here is what I am asking. To every team principal, every chief executive and the leaders of Formula 1 and the FIA: let's make the three recommendations in this report happen."
F1 last month published its first sport-wide social impact report.

It showed that more than 500,000 young people across 71 countries accessed and benefitted from Formula 1 programmes in education and community outreach in 2025, while over 2,500 young people took part in activities at F1 race tracks.
It also announced a three-year extension to its engineering scholarship until at least 2028/29, committing to a further £2.4m in funding.

That report added the sport will "strengthen its approach to governance, measurement and reporting to better understand results, share progress and maximise the long-term value of its social impact work".
An F1 spokesperson said: "We are proud of the programmes and initiatives which help inspire the next generation of Formula 1 and how they continue to increase access and opportunity across our sport.

"Following recommendations from the Hamilton Commission, the sport signed its first ever D&I charter in 2024, and in 2025, conducted its first ever sport wide data gathering exercise to capture the global reach of our social impact programmes.

"This showed that in the 2025 season alone, more than 500,000 young people engaged in education, STEM and inspiration programmes globally and over 1,000 structured skills and talent development opportunities across our sport.

"As Formula 1 continues to grow on the global stage, so too does our ambition to deepen and evolve our social impact. We are committed, alongside the F1 teams, the FIA and broader members of our sport to continue building on this foundation and look forward to sharing the next phase of our work."

Expressing his hopes for more progress in future, Hamilton said: "From engineering scholarships and the Diversity and Inclusion Charter to inspiring over 500,000 young people, we've helped drive real progress. I'm proud of what we've achieved, but we're nowhere near finished.

"Formula 1 is inspiring millions of young people around the world. But inspiration means nothing without opportunity. We can't tell young people to dream big and then not open the doors when they try to make those dreams a reality.

"F1, the FIA and every team must push harder and move faster. We need real investment, more opportunities and greater accountability. We've shown that change is possible. Now we need to go further. The talent is out there, and the future of our sport depends on unlocking it."

Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton wants a Los Angeles base so he can spend more of the winter break with his partner Kim Kardashian and her children, according to a report from the Daily Mail.

The report says the Ferrari driver approached estate agents about houses in Malibu, Pacific Palisades and the Hollywood Hills, and is weighing up whether to rent or buy. His main home is in Monaco, while Kardashian lives in Hidden Hills, a gated community north-west of central Los Angeles.

The couple have been linked since January, and Hamilton later shared photos of them together on social media. Kardashian has since become a familiar face in the paddock, watching him race in Monaco in June and in Singapore last month.
Hamilton has also spoken warmly about her children, North, Saint, Psalm and Chicago, from her marriage to rapper Kanye West.
At a fan event in Austin before last month's United States Grand Prix, he said: "My girlfriend's kids, I love spending time with them.
"She’s got four, so I’m getting to play with these kids. I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family."

This comes amid an up-and-down season for Hamilton. After a rocky first year with the Maranello outfit, he bounced back to his old race-winning form with the turn of the regulations. He secured his first podium with Ferrari at the Chinese Grand Prix and later celebrated his first grand prix win in red in Barcelona.
While Hamilton remains in the fight for second in the drivers' championship, power unit penalties and on-track clashes with his team-mate Charles Leclerc have marred the last few races.

With three races remaining in the season, Hamilton is fourth with 261 points, one point behind Mercedes' George Russell in third and 18 points behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second. Kimi Antonelli already secured the drivers' title at the Mexican Grand Prix.

What time the 2026 F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix starts across the US, plus the full schedule and how to watch live on Apple TV
The Las Vegas Grand Prix starts at 8 pm PT on Saturday, November 21, which is 11 pm ET. The race runs at night along the Strip, and every session is live on Apple TV.
In Alaska, every session starts one hour earlier than in the PT column, and in Hawaii two hours earlier. This is not a sprint weekend.
What time does the Las Vegas Grand Prix start?
The race starts on Saturday, November 21, at 8 pm PT, 9 pm MT, 10 pm CT and 11 pm ET. In Alaska, it starts at 7 pm, and in Hawaii at 6 pm

The race runs over 50 laps of the 3.853-mile street circuit, a total of 192.7 miles. Without interruptions, it finishes at around 9:30 pm PT, 12:30 am ET. If the race runs longer than two hours, the checkered flag falls at the two-hour mark even if not all laps are completed.
What time is Las Vegas GP qualifying?

Qualifying starts on Friday, November 20, at 8 pm PT, 11 pm ET, and lasts about an hour. The slowest five drivers drop out in Q1 and five more in Q2. The ten remaining drivers fight for pole position in Q3.
The cold desert night is the main challenge. Tires struggle to reach their working temperature on the long straights, and drivers who cannot switch them on in time lose big chunks of lap time.

All three Las Vegas practice sessions can be watched free on Apple TV without a subscription. Apple also makes selected race weekends available free, although it has not identified the Las Vegas Grand Prix as one of those free races.

What time the 2026 F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix starts in the UK, plus the full schedule and how to watch live on Sky Sports F1 and NOW
A rainbow above the Welcome to Las Vegas sign

The Las Vegas Grand Prix starts at 4am UK time on Sunday 22 November. In Las Vegas it is still 8pm on Saturday, because the race runs at night along the Strip. Every session falls overnight in the UK, and every one of them is live on Sky Sports F1.
Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 schedule in UK time
Las Vegas is eight hours behind the UK. This is not a sprint weekend.
What time does the Las Vegas Grand Prix start in the UK?

The Las Vegas Grand Prix starts at 4am UK time on Sunday 22 November. The race runs over 50 laps of the 6.201km (3.853-mile) street circuit, a total of 310km (192.7 miles). Without interruptions it finishes at around 5:30am. If the race runs longer than two hours, the chequered flag falls at the two-hour mark even if not all laps are completed.
What time is qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix?
Qualifying starts at 4am UK time on Saturday 21 November and lasts about an hour. The slowest five drivers drop out in Q1 and five more in Q2. The ten remaining drivers fight for pole position in Q3.

The cold night air is the main challenge in Las Vegas. Tyres struggle to reach their working temperature on the long straights, and drivers who cannot switch them on in time lose large chunks of lap time.
How to watch the Las Vegas Grand Prix in the UK

Sky Sports F1 shows every session live. Without a Sky TV subscription, the same coverage is available through NOW with no contract. Channel 4 shows free highlights of qualifying and the race a few hours after each session.
Every session live, for existing Sky TV customers
Live timing and replays, no live pictures
F1 TV Pro is not available in the UK. Sky holds the live UK rights.
What is at stake in Las Vegas?

Kimi Antonelli is already world champion and Mercedes has won the constructors' title. The fight for second place is wide open, and three British drivers are in it. Max Verstappen leads that battle on 279 points, ahead of George Russell on 262, Lewis Hamilton on 261, Charles Leclerc on 249 and Lando Norris on 246. With three races left, each driver can still score 75 points.
Norris won the last race in Brazil. In the constructors' championship, Red Bull on 415 points and McLaren on 398 are fighting for third.

The 6.201km street circuit runs past the casinos of the Las Vegas Strip, and its main straight is one of the fastest stretches on the calendar. The race starts at 8pm local time, when track temperatures drop sharply. That has decided the result here more than once.
Who won the Las Vegas Grand Prix in 2025?

Max Verstappen won the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Lando Norris started from pole and crossed the line second, but both McLarens were disqualified afterwards for excessive plank wear. George Russell and Kimi Antonelli completed the podium.

What time is the Las Vegas Grand Prix in the UK?
4am on Sunday 22 November. In Las Vegas it is 8pm on Saturday.
Is the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday or Sunday?
Both. It starts on Saturday evening in Las Vegas, which is early on Sunday morning in the UK.
Is the Las Vegas Grand Prix on free-to-air TV in the UK?
Not live. Channel 4 shows highlights of qualifying and the race. Live coverage is on Sky Sports F1 and NOW.
What time is qualifying in the UK?
4am on Saturday 21 November.
Is there a sprint race in Las Vegas?
No. The weekend has three practice sessions, qualifying and the Grand Prix.

detailZh: F1车手经纪人恩里科·扎纳里尼回顾赛车生涯五十年
恩里科·扎纳里尼回顾了自己与埃迪·埃尔文、亚历山德罗·扎纳尔迪和拉斐尔·卡马拉等人共事的半个世纪——处理人际关系、面对失望，以及一个发生了深刻变化的围场。这么多年过去，他仍然坚信一件事：即使在今天的F1，经验也是不可替代的资产。
有时，一个单一事件——仅仅几秒钟——就足以改变职业生涯的走向。恩里科·扎纳里尼回忆起这样一个时刻，它发生在1993年葡萄牙大奖赛的围场里。埃马努埃莱·纳斯佩蒂是扎纳里尼在20世纪90年代初管理的车手之一，当时正努力保住自己的F1未来。
目标是跑赢队友鲁本斯·巴里切罗——这样的成绩本可以增加他的机会。但在排位赛的决定性时刻，正当纳斯佩蒂全力冲击那可能改变他命运的一圈时，他发现刚出维修区的艾尔顿·塞纳正挡在身前。这次尝试被毁了，正如扎纳里尼所记得的那样，一个重大机会也随之消失。
“这是我们最后的机会，”扎纳里尼告诉Motorsport.com。“埃马努埃莱只剩最后一套轮胎，他必须全力以赴。当我看到塞纳从维修区驶出，而纳斯佩蒂正好到达最后一个弯角时，我就知道我们的圈速毁了。事实正是如此。”
恩里科·扎纳里尼与安东尼奥·吉奥维纳兹，哈斯F1车队
“我告诉自己，不能就这样结束，”他说。“我们必须再试一次——而且要做得更好。这成了我的座右铭之一，成了我生活和工作的原则之一。”
50年过去了，扎纳里尼依然活跃在围场之中。他跨越了不同的时代，认识了几代车手，与冠军和前途无量的年轻才俊都合作过。他的职业生涯始于1975年，当时他管理着一辆Autodelta赛车和两名车手。如今，他与弗朗切斯科·普林奇佩一起，代理的车手包括拉斐尔·卡马拉——后者刚刚代表哈斯完成F1首秀。
在这之间，是一生在赛车运动中度过的时光，而其中最鲜明的特点，是一种独特的经纪人工作方式。“在我们的世界里，你每一天都与车手朝夕相处，”他解释道，“你们会建立起非常紧密的纽带。和埃马努埃莱·纳斯佩蒂，我们就像兄弟一样——对他来说，我或许几乎像第二个父亲。而这些关系并不一定随着赛车生涯的结束而终止。”
最耐人寻味的例子是埃迪·欧文，他是在扎纳里尼职业道路上留下最深印记的车手之一：“埃迪真是把我折腾得够呛。他的情绪起伏极大，尤其是在私生活方面。但我们仍然是朋友。三十年过去了，如今——在巴西和拉斯维加斯之间——我们正一起在秘鲁度假一周。两个老家伙在度假！”
这是一种似乎属于另一个时代的经纪理念，但扎纳里尼仍然认为它至关重要——尤其是因为，在他看来，车手随着时间推移的变化，远没有人们想象的那么大。
他评价道：“纳斯佩蒂、欧文或扎纳尔迪所拥有的那种竞争力，我在今天的卡马拉身上同样能看到。一旦护目镜放下，他们都会变成充满竞争本能的猛兽。”
“最大的变化在于技术和社交媒体的影响。过去，与公众的关系完全不同。如今，年轻车手会花大量时间在手机上——了解信息、直接与人交流。但竞争精神始终如一。”
经验的价值以及与法拉利的关系
几十年来，经纪人的角色也经历了深刻变化。车队和制造商设立青训车队的做法改变了平衡，在某些情况下缩小了车手代表们的施展空间。
“在红牛——至少只要赫尔穆特·马尔科还在掌权——几乎不可能进行任何有意义的对话。他们甚至不会考虑你，除非你恰好是马克斯·维斯塔潘的经纪人。梅赛德斯也采取非常专断的方式，倾向于把经纪人晾在一边。相比之下，法拉利一直尊重我们的工作。哈斯和迈凯伦也是如此。”
与马拉内罗的关系是该经纪公司的一大优势。这段合作始于欧文时代，并延续至今，目前扎纳里尼的公司代理着五名与法拉利有关联的车手。这也是卡马拉将职业生涯托付给该公司的原因。
“拉斐尔来找我们，是因为他想要那种与法拉利建立长期关系所带来的经验，”扎纳里尼解释道。“我们早就认识他，也一直饶有兴趣地关注他的进展，但我们没有主动追求他，因为他当时有另一位经纪人。这是职业道德问题；我们尊重他人的工作。”
道德这个话题在扎纳里尼的叙述中反复出现。“这是一个很容易搞暗箱操作的环境——你可以通过违规操作快速赚钱，”他补充道。“我一直告诉我的团队要行为端正，按规矩办事。这也是你如何长期维持关系的方式。”
扎纳里尼认为，经验是管理者能给予年轻车手的最宝贵财富：“你不必是天才。当你在赛车运动里摸爬滚打50年，你见过太多场景，它们迟早会重演。20年前发生的事，明天早上就可能同样发生在拉斐尔身上。我能让他做好准备，告诉他该期待什么。而且他是个聪明的年轻人，非常尊重经验。”
“在拉斐尔这件事上，我们与巴西一家商业伙伴——FWD经纪公司——的联系也起了关键作用；他们在卡马拉项目上做得非常出色。一切完美地衔接上了。”
为卡马拉在巴西大奖赛完成F1首秀做准备，需要一套特定的方法。在职业生涯一直追逐杆位、分站胜利和年度冠军之后，这位新秀突然发现自己身处一个成功标准完全不同的环境。
“过去一周，我们不得不把一切推倒重来，”扎纳里尼解释道。“我们所在的这支车队——除非出现某些非同寻常的变故——不会去争夺杆位或分站胜利。拉斐尔习惯了为胜利而战，所以我们必须向他解释，如今工作的性质不同了。如果他做得好，总有一天他会拥有一辆能够拿下杆位和胜利的赛车。”
恩里科·扎纳里尼与吉安卡洛·费斯切拉
对扎纳里尼而言，进入F1并不仅仅是一段旅程的顶点，而是一个新篇章的开始。当被问及他管理过的车手中，谁在纯粹天赋上与卡马拉最相似时，他的回答很能说明问题：“也许是[吉安卡洛]费斯切拉。很难做比较，但就纯粹天赋而言，他是第一个浮现在我脑海里的。不过他们的性格完全不同——一个内向，一个外向。”
经理人工作中还有一个很少被关注的方面：管理车手的家庭。“我们实际上已经拿到了‘家长管理’的学位！”扎纳里尼感叹道，“我觉得我们应该得一个特别奖。有时候，管理父母比管理车手更费心。家庭为了帮助孩子达到这些水平牺牲了很多，情感纽带非常牢固。但到了某个阶段，年轻车手需要变得独立，引导这一转变并不总是容易的。”
从罗恩·丹尼斯到扎克·布朗，一个不那么傲慢的围场
扎纳里尼经历过一种F1，在那个世界里，决定由车队老板直接做出——个人关系往往具有决定性，尽管并不总是那么简单直接。
他回忆起与罗恩·丹尼斯的一次会面，那次会面是为了在吉安卡洛·费斯切拉赢得2003年巴西大奖赛后讨论他：“他在伊莫拉附近的酒店房间里接待了我。他从一开始就很傲慢。他告诉我他对费斯切拉不感兴趣，他之所以同意见我，只是因为是我提出的请求。告诉别人你不感兴趣有不同的方式，而他显然没有选择最优雅的那种……”
与迈凯伦现任领导层的对比十分鲜明：“扎克·布朗的精神与我很相似。我总是说我是个二手车销售员，因为我来自那个行业。而当你在展厅工作时，你会学到必须倾听每一个人。可能走进来一个看起来身无分文的人，最后却买了三辆梅赛德斯。扎克倾听每一个人，然后，自然而然地，他得出自己的结论。”
矛盾的是，尽管F1变得复杂和富裕得多，如今在扎纳里尼看来，它却不像过去那样傲慢了：“那时候，有个人所有者；今天，结构不同了，对话也更多了。我在今天的围场里看不到当年我有时会遇到的那种傲慢。”
扎纳里尼对伯尼·埃克莱斯顿时代与自由媒体时代的比较同样不带怀旧情绪。他承认旧体系在当时行之有效，但认为当前的管理层更适合F1如今达到的规模。
安东尼奥·吉奥维纳齐、哈斯F1车队和恩里科·扎纳里尼
从业50年后，扎纳里尼毫无放慢脚步的迹象。当被问及是否曾考虑离开赛车运动时，他立刻回答：“没有——因为第二天我就会死！”
然而，他也意识到经纪公司的未来最终必须托付给新一代。弗朗切斯科·普林奇佩正是在此背景下登场，他被赋予了负责卡马拉项目的职责。
“这个项目完全掌握在他手中，这让我感到无比欣慰，”扎纳里尼说道。“弗朗切斯科·普林奇佩在某种意义上是我自己的创造——我自豪地这么说。我们形成了一种共生关系，他新鲜、年轻的心态与我的经验相辅相成。”
这种纽带超越了职业层面：“我自己的孩子选择了不同的职业道路。在赛车运动的世界里，弗朗切斯科就是我的儿子。我知道我自己的旅程终有一天会结束，但知道会有人将这项工作传承下去，这让我感到欣慰。”
或许这段话最能概括恩里科·扎纳里尼的故事——一个见证了赛车、车队、规则以及赛车运动商业运作方式演变的人。他认识那些后来赢得世界冠军的车手，也认识那些在排位赛刚跑出几米就梦想破灭的人。
而半个世纪后的今天，他依然在那两个曾出现在电视屏幕上的词中看到自己的影子——那是一个格外苦涩的下午：“再努力些。”再试一次——并且做得更好。
detailEn: F1 driver manager Enrico Zanarini recounts his 50 years in motorsport

Enrico Zanarini reflects on half a century spent working alongside the likes of Eddie Irvine, Alessandro Zanardi and Rafael Camara – navigating personal relationships, disappointments, and a profoundly transformed paddock. After all this time, he remains convinced of one thing: experience is an irreplaceable asset, even in today’s F1

Sometimes, a single incident – mere seconds – is enough to alter the course of a career. Enrico Zanarini recalls one such moment, which took place in the paddock at the 1993 Portuguese Grand Prix. Emanuele Naspetti, one of the drivers Zanarini managed in the early 1990s, was striving to secure his Formula 1 future.

The goal was to outperform his team-mate, Rubens Barrichello – a result that could have bolstered his chances. But at the decisive moment during qualifying, just as Naspetti was pushing for the lap that might have changed his destiny, he found Ayrton Senna – who had just exited the pits – directly in his path. The attempt was ruined, and with it, as Zanarini remembers, a major opportunity vanished.

“It was our last chance,” Zanarini told Motorsport.com. “Emanuele had one final set of tires left, and he absolutely had to deliver. When I saw Senna pulling out of the pits just as Naspetti was reaching the final corner, I knew our lap was ruined. And that is exactly what happened.”

Zanarini returned to the paddock, devastated. He absent-mindedly sat down in front of a television, before noticing a Nike commercial. He didn’t pay much attention to the visuals, but the words that appeared at the end stayed with him: “Try Harder” – raise the bar.
Enrico Zanarini and Antonio Giovinazzi, Haas F1 Team
“I told myself it couldn’t end like this,” he said. “We had to give it another try – and do it better. That became one of my mottos, one of the principles by which I live and work.”

After 50 years, Zanarini is still in the paddock. He has spanned different eras, known generations of drivers, and worked with both champions and promising young talents. His career began in 1975, when he managed an Autodelta car and two drivers. Today, alongside Francesco Principe, he represents – among others – Rafael Camara, who has just made his F1 debut with Haas.

In between lies a lifetime spent in motorsport, defined above all by a unique approach to the manager job. “In our world, you live alongside the drivers every single day,” he explained. “You form very close bonds. With Emanuele Naspetti, we were like brothers – to him, I was perhaps almost a second father. And these are relationships that don’t necessarily end when a racing career does.”

The most intriguing example is Eddie Irvine, one of the drivers who left the deepest marks on Zanarini’s professional journey: “Eddie really put me through the wringer. He had incredible mood swings, especially when it came to his private life. Yet, we’re still friends. Thirty years have passed, and now – between Brazil and Las Vegas – we’re vacationing together in Peru for a week. Two old guys on holiday!”

It is a philosophy of management that seems to belong to another era, yet Zanarini still considers it essential – not least because, in his view, drivers have changed far less over time than one might imagine.
“The competitiveness that Naspetti, Irvine, or Zanardi possessed is the same I see in Camara today,” he reckoned. “Once the visor goes down, they all turn into competitive animals.

“What has changed, above all, is the influence of technology and social media. In the past, the relationship with the public was completely different. Today, a young driver spends a lot of time on his phone – staying informed, communicating directly with people. But the competitive spirit remains the same.”
The value of experience and the relationship with Ferrari

Over the decades, the role of a manager has also undergone profound change. The emergence of academies run by teams and manufacturers has shifted the balance, in some cases narrowing the scope for those who represent the drivers.

“With Red Bull – at least as long as Helmut Marko was in charge – it was practically impossible to engage in any meaningful dialogue. They wouldn’t even consider you, unless you happened to be Max Verstappen’s manager. Mercedes also takes a very authoritarian approach, tending to keep managers on the sidelines. Ferrari, by contrast, has always respected our work. The same can be said for Haas and McLaren.”

The relationship with Maranello is one of the agency’s key strengths. It is a partnership that began back in the Irvine days and lives on, with five Ferrari-linked drivers currently represented by Zanarini’s organisation. This was also why Camara trusted the agency with his career.

“Rafael came to us because he was looking for the experience that comes with an established relationship with Ferrari,” Zanarini explained. “We already knew him and had been following his progress with interest, but we didn’t actively pursue him because he had another manager. It’s a matter of professional ethics; we respect the work of others.”

The subject of ethics comes up repeatedly in Zanarini’s account. “This is an environment where it’s easy to engage in underhanded practices – where you could make quick money by operating outside the rules,” he added. “I’ve always told my team to conduct themselves properly and to do things the right way. That is also how you maintain relationships over time.”

According to Zanarini, experience is the greatest asset a manager can offer a young driver: “You don’t have to be a genius. When you’ve spent 50 years in motorsport, you’ve seen so many scenarios that, sooner or later, are bound to repeat themselves. Something that happened 20 years ago could just as easily happen to Rafael tomorrow morning. I can prepare him and explain what to expect. And he’s an intelligent young man who has a great deal of respect for experience.

“In Rafael’s case, a connection we have with a commercial partner in Brazil – agency FWD – also played a crucial role; they are doing an excellent job with the Camara project. Everything fell into place perfectly.”

Preparing Camara for his F1 debut at the Brazilian GP required a specific approach. After a career built on chasing pole positions, race wins and championship titles, the rookie suddenly found himself in an environment where success is measured by entirely different criteria.

“Over the last week, we’ve had to reset everything,” Zanarini explained. “We’re with a team where – barring some extraordinary turn of events – we won’t be taking pole positions or winning races. Rafael is used to fighting for wins, so we’ve had to explain to him that the nature of the work is different now. If he does a good job, the time will come when he’ll have a car capable of securing pole positions and victories.”
Enrico Zanarini with Giancarlo Fisichella

For Zanarini, reaching F1 isn’t just the culmination of a journey; it’s the start of a new chapter. And when asked which of the drivers he has managed was most similar to Camara in terms of raw talent, his answer is telling: “Perhaps [Giancarlo] Fisichella. It’s very difficult to make comparisons, but in terms of pure talent, he’s the one who comes to mind. Their personalities, however, are completely different – one is introverted, the other extroverted.”

There is also an aspect of a manager’s job that rarely comes to light: managing the families. “We’ve practically earned a degree in ‘parent management’!” Zanarini exclaimed. “I think we deserve a special award. Sometimes, managing the parents is more demanding than managing the drivers. Families have sacrificed so much to help their children reach these levels, and the emotional bond is incredibly strong. But there comes a point when the young driver needs to become independent, and guiding that transition isn’t always easy.”
From Ron Dennis to Zak Brown, a less arrogant paddock
Zanarini experienced a version of F1 where decisions were made directly by team owners – a world where personal relationships were often decisive, albeit not always straightforward.

He recalls a meeting with Ron Dennis, arranged to discuss Giancarlo Fisichella following his victory at the 2003 Brazilian GP: “He received me in his hotel room, near Imola. He was arrogant right from the start. He told me he wasn’t interested in Fisichella and he had only agreed to meet me because I had asked him to. There are different ways to tell someone you’re not interested, and he certainly didn’t choose the most elegant one…”

The contrast with McLaren’s current leadership is stark: “Zak Brown has a very similar spirit to mine. I always say that I’m a used-car salesman, because that’s the industry I come from. And when you work in a showroom, you learn that you have to listen to everyone. Someone might walk in who looks like they don’t have a penny to their name, and then end up buying three Mercedes. Zak listens to everyone, and then, naturally, he draws his own conclusions.”

Paradoxically, even though F1 has become much more complex and affluent, it now strikes Zanarini as less arrogant than it used to be: “Back then, there were individual owners; today, the structures are different, and there is more dialogue. I don’t see the same kind of arrogance in today’s paddock that I sometimes encountered back then.”

Zanarini’s comparison between the Bernie Ecclestone era and the Liberty Media era is also devoid of nostalgia. While he acknowledges that the old system worked at the time, he believes the current management is far better-suited to the scale that F1 has reached.
Antonio Giovinazzi, Haas F1 Team and Enrico Zanarini
After 50 years in the business, Zanarini shows no signs of slowing down. When asked if he has ever considered leaving motorsport, his reply is immediate: “No – because the very next day, I’d die!”

Yet, there is an awareness that the future of the agency must eventually be entrusted to a new generation. This is where Francesco Principe enters the picture, having been given responsibility for the Camara project.

“This project is entirely in his hands, which gives me immense satisfaction,” Zanarini said. “Francesco Principe is, in a sense, my own creation – I say that with pride. We’ve developed a symbiosis where his fresh, youthful mindset complements my own experience.”

The bond goes beyond professional matters: “My own children chose different career paths. In the world of motorsport, Francesco is my son. I know that my own journey will come to an end one day, but it’s comforting to know that there will be someone to carry this work forward.”

Perhaps this passage best encapsulates the story of Enrico Zanarini – a man who has witnessed the evolution of race cars, teams, regulations, and the very way business is conducted in motorsport. He has known drivers who went on to win world championships, as well as others who saw their dreams vanish just meters into a qualifying lap.

And now, half a century later, he still finds himself reflected in those two words that once appeared on a television screen on a particularly bitter afternoon: “Try Harder.” Try again – and try better.
